rationale: Evidence across cohorts indicates that neither optic atrophy nor epileptic seizures are 100% penetrant obligate features in all PLAA-variant individuals. Hall et al. explicitly noted that 'most' rather than all patients developed seizures and described progressive or variable visual/optic atrophy manifestations. Furthermore, evaluations by Chitre et al. and Sabaie et al. demonstrated that PLAA mutations can manifest as PEHO or PEHO-like presentations with notable variability in ophthalmological involvement (optic atrophy) and seizure semiology even within families, supporting the hypothesis that these features define a variable, severe PEHO-like subset rather than invariant 100% penetrant diagnostic requirements.

evidence.text: Hall et al. described hypomorphic PLAA variants in an infantile neurodysfunction syndrome where optic atrophy developed in the first year and most, but not all, individuals had seizures.

evidence.text: In a cohort of 19 children with PEHO and PEHO-like phenotypes, a pathogenic PLAA variant (c.68G>T, p.Gly23Val) was identified, and the authors highlighted significant variation in ophthalmological and MRI features even among individuals with the same underlying molecular diagnoses, questioning whether optic atrophy should remain an essential diagnostic criterion.

source.quote: They were similar in many of the core and the supporting features of PEHO, but there was significant variation in MRI and ophthalmological findings, even between siblings with the same mutation.

evidence.text: Sabaie et al. reviewed PEHO and PEHO-like syndromes, reporting that optic atrophy and infantile spasms/seizures show inconsistent presence across genetically defined cohorts that include genes such as PLAA.

source.title: Clinical and genetic features of PEHO and PEHO-Like syndromes: A scoping review
source.quote: Cerebellar atrophy was the main clinical difference between the two groups but data on optic atrophy and infantile spasms/hypsarrhythmia were not consistent with the previously essential diagnostic criteria.

new_directions.question_text: What is the exact penetrance of optic atrophy and epileptic seizures across all molecularly confirmed biallelic PLAA cases in international registries?
new_directions.rationale: Collating all reported PLAA cases outside dedicated PEHO-only ascertainment cohorts will clarify the true frequency and age-dependent penetrance of optic atrophy and distinct seizure types.

new_directions.question_text: Do N-terminal PLAA missense variants alter endolysosomal synaptic protein clearance differently than truncating or C-terminal variants in human iPSC-derived cortical neurons?
new_directions.rationale: Differences in residual ubiquitin-binding or endolysosomal sorting activity might explain why some patients exhibit early infantile epileptic encephalopathy with optic atrophy while others display predominantly spastic paraplegia or leukoencephalopathy.
